issue_context.title: `push_error` is hiding prints in editor output
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.1.1.stable.official [bd6af8e0e]

### System information

Godot v4.1.1.stable - Windows 10.0.22621 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.3713) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900X 12-Core Processor (24 Threads)

### Issue description

`push_error` is hiding other prints in the editor output. The output counter are still showing the correct count. Choosing a different  message type filter refreshes the view and will show the hidden message.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a scene with a node and attach a script with content:

```gdscript
@tool
extends Node2D

func _ready():
	print("hello world")
	push_error("test")
	print("bye world")
```

Reload the scene and only
```
  ./core/variant/variant_utility.cpp:905 - test
hello world
```
is shown.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
I can repro that, but it seems somewhat random. At first I couldn't repro this, but after a few scene close+open it started happening, tested on current master too. Happens more often after clearing the log output window. Same as OP, two lines are posted but the message count shows 2 standard messages (where `"bye world"` is not visible) and 1 error message.

There have been a few somewhat similar issues with the log output, including some RichTextLabel thread related problems. Could be related.
I've seen this happen outside of godot too, usually because stderr and stdout are writing to the console in parallel, and so you get weird errors like that.

In my windows machine, `push_error` and `print` both goes into `WindowsTerminalLogger::logv` ：
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/59139df16e7a10c3b9176f697d23b557af46601e/platform/windows/windows_terminal_logger.cpp#L66-L70

The second `print` will call `wprintf`, but the result is not shown in the output window even with a fflush everytime, but the message will show in the console though. So it's probably not because stderr and stdout are writing to the console in parallel, it could be a RichTextLabel related problem.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/8315986/e09026c5-6f68-470a-91c6-e162243f64d7)


Update: I think I found the culprit: 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/549fcce5f8f7beace3e5c90e9bbe4335d4fd1476/editor/editor_log.cpp#L284-L287

At least we can have a message queue or something like that ?  Just return will cause the log disappear.
@bruvzg Any ideas?
I am trying ues a new timer to fix that issue. Do you have any better suggestions?

I was thinking about something like push the meassge to a a lock-free queue or just block here to wait for updating to finish. 

There might be a more simple way of doing this, anyway I think lag is fine but the log should not disappear.
